# introduction
Read the guidelines at .github/copilot-instructions. You have the role of reviewer, you will write plans for analyzer and then start an analyzer subagent to carry out that those plans. It is up to you how to schedule and send off the tasks to analyzer subagent(s), but keep the work of each subagent isolated. Be careful of recompiling executables which might be in use by another program. If there is a chance a file is being edited or executable ran or will soon-to-be ran by anther subagent, then wait until that subagent's task has concluded. For analysis production use 20-30 threads, for skimming use 5 threads for mc and 10 threads for data.


# follow ups on energy extrapolation
Looking at the recent energy extrapolation plots we can see the energy weight has the opposite effect than we expect. Generally we would see a deapening of the deltaeta correlation. The track correction interestingly encodes this, but adding the energy weight to the mix (Z+track resiudal+energy extrapolation), we get a less deep deltaeta feature which is the opposite effect we expect. Indeed looking back to previous iterations of the pp energy weight we see the energy weight is the dominant factor and deepens the deltaeta feature. Ensure the energy weight is applied correctly. We calculate the energy weight as a ratio between data Z pt spectra (w ~ 8.16 TeV pPb / 5.02 TeV pp) and the weight should be applied multiplicatively to pp 5.02 data. Furthermore ensure when we make those plots in the energy extrapolation section that each curve progressively applied corrections to pp 5.02 TeV data i.e. no correction (but still VZ correction, event weight, etc.), Z correction, Z and track correction, Z and track and energy correction). The effect of applying the track residual correction also looks a bit too large here, so that can be looked into too. Make sure the new track residual calculation method (going up to only 15 GeV in trk pT) was propagated to the refreshed energy weights. Confirm the current energy plots in the note are the current ones. If energy weights are recalculated then propagate the new weights to the pp curves in ALL result plots, as well as ALL pp systematics. Copy over to the overleaf any plots that change. Return with a summary of what was done.



# conclusion
Make the minimum number of edits necessary to implement functionality. Do not add superflous error statement catches or checks. 

Have the subanalyzer handoff a summary to you and you should review that summary for flaws. Update copilot instructions on the new norms detailed here and learned by you or the subanalyzer throught these tasks.
